newsitem.title: UK: UK industry chief criticises Labour policies.
newsitem.headline: UK industry chief criticises Labour policies.

text.p: The head of British employers' organisation the Institute Of Directors on Wednesday said the Labour Party could be damaging to industry and jobs if it won next week's election.

Tim Melville-Ross, director general of the IOD, said Labour policies on a minimum wage and plans to end Britain's opt-out of the European Union's social chapter would increase unemployment and fuel inflation.

Ross, speaking at the IOD's annual convention, also expressed concern about Labour's stance on trade union legislation. "We had rather taken the point that the 1980s legislation would not be reversed, but now there's talk of compulsory recognition of trade unions."
He said it was worrying that there was so much uncertainty on Labour's policies on tax, privatisation and the European single currency.
"There is so much uncertainty about what a Labour government would do...this has to be resolved as quickly as possible."
Labour, in opposition since 1979, has been trying to reassure industry that its policies will be business-friendly and not a return to the tax-and-spend days of the 1970s. The election is on May 1.
Melville-Ross said his criticisms did not mean the IOD was not prepared to work with a Labour government and the organisation also had criticisms of the ruling Conservatives' policies.
"There are still some real concerns...about the level of public expenditure and the level of the public sector borrowing requirement at this late stage in the recovery," he later told journalists.
